answer: Admission runs through a narrow inlet: every new identity must be carried in by a sponsor's ember, a one-use burn receipt that regrows only after a full epoch of honest work. A velvet rope then binds sponsor and newcomer: if the newcomer cheats, the sponsor's own stake is slashed by the square of the number of bad vouches issued, so ten clones cost their sponsor a hundredfold penalty. One ember admits one identity only, and a sponsor who spends ember faster than it regrows is locked out of the inlet, so a farm's cost grows faster than its size while an honest sponsor keeps the ember warm.
